questions.question: A developer accepts a GitHub Copilot suggestion for a function that calculates order discounts. What is the most reliable way to confirm that the function behaves correctly?

options.text: Run unit tests that include edge cases, such as an unknown discount code
options.why: Correct. Running tests with edge cases verifies behavior directly instead of relying on appearance.

options.text: Ask Copilot Chat whether the function is correct
options.why: Copilot can help explain code, but its answer is another prediction, not verification.

options.text: Confirm that the code compiles without errors
options.why: Compilation confirms syntax only. Logic errors can still exist.

options.text: Regenerate the suggestion and compare the two versions
options.why: Comparing two predictions does not verify that either one is correct.

questions.explanation: AI output must be validated. Tests with edge cases are the most direct way to confirm behavior.

questions.question: A repository requires that AI-assisted code be checked for security vulnerabilities before it is merged. Which control should you add to the pull request workflow?

options.text: Code scanning with CodeQL as a required status check
options.why: Correct. Code scanning analyzes code for vulnerabilities and can block merges when it is a required check.

options.text: A larger premium request allowance
options.why: Premium requests affect model usage, not security analysis.

options.text: Next edit suggestions in the IDE
options.why: Next edit suggestions predict edits. They do not scan for vulnerabilities.

options.text: A prompt file that asks Copilot to write secure code
options.why: Prompting may improve output but does not verify it.

questions.explanation: Code scanning detects security issues that tests often miss and is a key validation step for AI-generated code.

questions.question: A team adds GitHub Copilot as a reviewer on every pull request. The repository requires one approving review before merge. Which statement is true?

options.text: Copilot leaves comments and suggested changes, and a human approval is still required
options.why: Correct. Copilot code review does not approve pull requests or count toward required approvals.

options.text: Copilot's review satisfies the required approval
options.why: Copilot code review leaves Comment reviews only and does not count toward required approvals.

options.text: Copilot can request changes and block the merge
options.why: Copilot does not submit Request changes reviews.

options.text: Copilot merges the pull request automatically when its review passes
options.why: Copilot code review does not merge pull requests.

questions.explanation: Human review remains part of responsible operation. Copilot code review is an additional reviewer, not an approver.

questions.question: Which THREE practices are part of operating GitHub Copilot responsibly?

options.text: Review and understand each suggestion before accepting it
options.why: Correct. Developers must understand code they accept and maintain.

options.text: Exclude secrets and real personal data from prompts
options.why: Correct. Prompts are sent to the service, so sensitive data should not be included.

options.text: Keep pull request reviews and CI checks in place for AI-assisted code
options.why: Correct. Existing safeguards still apply to code that Copilot helped write.

options.text: Accept long suggestions without reading them to save time
options.why: Unreviewed code can introduce bugs and vulnerabilities.

options.text: Rely on Copilot-generated tests as the only validation of Copilot-generated code
options.why: Tests from the same model can share the same incorrect assumptions.

questions.explanation: Responsible use combines understanding, data protection and the normal review and CI safeguards.

questions.scenario: A developer uses the /tests command to generate tests for a Copilot-written applyDiscount function. All generated tests pass. In production, an unknown discount code returns NaN.
questions.question: What is the most likely reason the tests did not detect the defect?

options.text: The generated tests shared the same assumption as the code and did not cover an unknown code
options.why: Correct. Tests produced from the same context can miss the same edge cases as the code.

options.text: The /tests command cannot generate tests for JavaScript
options.why: /tests can generate tests for JavaScript and many other languages.

options.text: Copilot does not allow tests to run in the terminal
options.why: Tests run with the project's own test runner, such as npm test.

options.text: The public code filter removed the failing test
options.why: The public code filter acts on suggestions that match public code, not on test coverage.

questions.explanation: Review generated tests and add edge cases yourself, so that code and tests do not share one blind spot.
